source_issues: The 'Percussion' leaf reports palpation-type findings ('Abdomen is soft, non-distended'); the result drops the percussion label.
Jaundice of the conjunctivae and skin is recorded under Abdominal_Examination.Inspection.
No test images or samples the pancreas (no CT, CA 19-9 or biopsy); the diagnosis rests on painless obstructive jaundice with a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier sign) and duct dilation.
All four vital signs are given only as 'Normal'.
notes: The 2-week duration covers both jaundice and itching, so it is a standalone fact (f004); 'gradual' is kept on the yellowing (f002).
The conjunctival and skin jaundice leaf (e005) is its own record (x005), because a doctor requests inspection for jaundice separately from the abdominal exam.
Alcohol is split into current abstinence (f013, absent) and past use (f014, historical); 'History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking' (PMH) merges with these and with smoking (f015).
Gold aliases leave out 'pancreatic cancer' and 'pancreatic carcinoma', which also cover non-adenocarcinoma tumours (broader); the judge can give credit.
Gold aliases added in harmonisation (pancreatic cancer, pancreatic carcinoma): 'Pancreatic cancer' is the everyday name of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (about 90% of pancreatic cancers).

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess the patient and determine the cause of jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stool, and dark urine.
